entries.land_location_as_stated: on the shore of Silver Lake, in the rapidly suburbanizing South Shore area of Massachusetts
entries.description: A 100-acre farm with woods, swamp, cranberry bog, and gardens on Silver Lake in Massachusetts, run and inhabited by a couple. They offer camping and farmwork experience to women and children, longer-term apprenticeships, and are organizing resources for a land trust. They explicitly reject lesbian separatism.
entries.raw_text: FEATHERS FARM Box 19, Bryantville, MA 02327 (617)585-3826. My partner & I are the only residents of Feathers Farm, 100 acres of woods, swamp, cranberry bog & gardens on the shore of Silver Lake, in the rapidly suburbanizing South Shore area of Massachusetts. We have camping facilities/open space/ farmwork experience to women and children. We are currently working to organize support and resources for a land trust to control this property. We have found lesbian separatism to be unworkable and alienating approach to this endeavor and expect unconditional acceptance of this from our visitors (whom we welcome AND encourage). We request that visitors bring their own food & donate $4/night camping fee, flexible. We often work out other arrangements for longer term apprenticeships or short term large groups. It is helpful if visits are preceeded by at least a phone-call, preferably a letter.
entries.notes: Type is Private/Individual Land under the two-woman rule ('My partner & I are the only residents of Feathers Farm'); a land trust is only currently being organized. Accepted groups inferred from 'women and children' in a pre-1986 directory. Focuses are Farming/self-sufficiency ('cranberry bog & gardens', 'farmwork experience') and Workshops/education ('apprenticeships'). Separatism is explicitly rejected ('found lesbian separatism to be unworkable and alienating approach') and therefore not coded as a focus.

entries.description: An intentional community on 113 acres of mountains and woodland in Troy, Maine, with four resident lesbians. They offer parcels for sale or building, camping, and hiking, and welcome new members, non-lesbian women, girl children, and lesbians interested in buying land.
entries.raw_text: WOMONGROUND Rt 1, Box 2420, Troy, ME 04987. 113 acres of Maine mountains/woodland. Parcels available for sale and/or building. Also plenty of space for camping, hiking, raspberry picking. Will answer all letters promptly. We welcome: new members/residents, girl children, nonlesbian women, lesbians interested in buying land. We have/are: 4 lesbians, 113 acres, housing/permanent structures, camping space, woods, women working and living on the land.
entries.notes: Land address inferred from rural route mailing address. Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative based on four resident lesbians living on the land and recruiting new members. Accepted groups coded from explicit welcome list: 'girl children, nonlesbian women, lesbians interested in buying land'.

entries.description: A 20-acre collective property in Vermont with two dwellings built by dykes, currently rented to heterosexuals because none of the dyke collective owners live there. They are seeking lesbian renters.
entries.raw_text: GENEROUS EARTH LAND Box 51A, Hinesburg, VT 05461. 20 acres, creek, woods, open. 2 dyke-built dwellings, one large, one small. No plumbing or electricity. None of the dyke collective owners live there now. It's rented to hets. Interested in dyke renters. 15 miles from town with jobs. Write before visiting.
entries.notes: Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative based on ownership by a 'dyke collective'. Number of residents is 0 ('None of the dyke collective owners live there now'). Accepted groups includes Lesbian women based on 'Interested in dyke renters'. PO box address does not give land street address.

entries.description: A working homestead farm in Vermont offering year-round retreat and temporary living space, cross-country ski weekends, and summer work exchanges. They have an all-lesbian maple sugar bush, draft horse, dairy goats, and chickens, and welcome community members and women wanting to lease land or take workshops.
entries.raw_text: GREENHOPE Box 226, E Hardwick, VT 05836. (802)533-7772. At present we are a working homestead farm. We offer year round space to women needing retreat or temporary living situation. We have gorgeous secluded land and campsites. Hope to build visitor cabins this summer. Women from the Boston area visit almost every weekend. Right now we are offering x-country ski weekends — $35 plus meals is the fee. In summer we offer work exchange. We have an all lesbian maple sugar bush — the only one I know of. We work with a draft horse, raise dairy goats and chickens. We are vegetarians raising nearly all our food organically here. We welcome community members and will lease land to women wanting to build a cabin or tipi.We offer workshops in
entries.notes: Type is Retreat/Gathering Space because retreat is named first ('space to women needing retreat') and the primary focus is hosting visitors and ski weekends. Accepted groups include Lesbian women and Non-lesbian women from 'women' in a pre-1986 listing. Focuses are Farming/self-sufficiency ('homestead farm', 'dairy goats and chickens') and Workshops/education ('We offer workshops in'). The listing continues onto the following page.
